titulo: Understanding the Past and Human Experiences
titulo_es: Comprender el pasado y la experiencia humana
estandares: Relaciono experiencias pasadas con el presente y las ordeno en el tiempo con precisión. Reflexiono sobre mi trayectoria personal y la de otros usando estructuras complejas.
competencias: Distinguir presente perfecto y pasado perfecto en sus formas simple y continua; emplear con precisión for, since, already, yet, just, ever y never; describir carácter, emociones y experiencias.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante escribe y presenta la trayectoria de una persona (real o propia) en tres capítulos: lo que había ocurrido antes, lo que ha vivido hasta hoy y cómo eso lo define.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student writes and presents the trajectory of a person (real or their own) in three chapters: what had happened before, what they have lived through until today and how that defines them.

lecciones.content_es:
Simple: have/has + participio

Se enfoca en el resultado o en la experiencia: I have written three essays this semester.

Continuo: have/has been + -ing

Se enfoca en la duración o en el proceso, que puede seguir: I have been writing all afternoon.

Cómo elegir

  • Con cantidad exacta → simple: She has read four books.
  • Con duración (for, since, all day, lately) → continuo: She has been reading since noon.
  • Con efecto visible en el presente → continuo: You've been crying, haven't you?
  • Con verbos de estado (know, be, have) → siempre simple.

Con live, work y study

Ambas formas son equivalentes: I've worked here for five years = I've been working here for five years.
lecciones.content_en:
Simple: have/has + participle

It focuses on the result or the experience: I have written three essays this semester.

Continuous: have/has been + -ing

It focuses on the duration or the process, which may still be going: I have been writing all afternoon.

How to choose

  • With an exact quantity → simple: She has read four books.
  • With duration (for, since, all day, lately) → continuous: She has been reading since noon.
  • With a visible present effect → continuous: You've been crying, haven't you?
  • With state verbs (know, be, have) → always simple.

With live, work and study

Both forms are equivalent: I've worked here for five years = I've been working here for five years.

lecciones.content_es:
Simple: had + participio

Una acción terminada antes de otro momento pasado: When she arrived, they had left.

Continuo: had been + -ing

Una acción en curso hasta ese momento pasado, con énfasis en la duración: She was tired because she had been working for ten hours.

La misma lógica de siempre

  • Resultado o cantidad → simple: He had sent three messages before she replied.
  • Duración o causa visible → continuo: The ground was wet; it had been raining.

Con for y since

By 2020 they had been living abroad for a decade.

Ojo

Los verbos de estado tampoco admiten el continuo aquí: She had known him since childhood.
lecciones.content_en:
Simple: had + participle

An action finished before another past moment: When she arrived, they had left.

Continuous: had been + -ing

An action in progress up to that past moment, with the focus on duration: She was tired because she had been working for ten hours.

The same logic as always

  • Result or quantity → simple: He had sent three messages before she replied.
  • Duration or visible cause → continuous: The ground was wet; it had been raining.

With for and since

By 2020 they had been living abroad for a decade.

Careful

State verbs take no continuous here either: She had known him since childhood.

lecciones.t: Presente perfecto vs pasado perfecto vs pasado simple
lecciones.t_en: Present perfect vs past perfect vs past simple
lecciones.content_es:
Cada uno con su punto de referencia

  • Pasado simple → un momento terminado del pasado: I graduated in 2024.
  • Presente perfecto → conecta con el ahora: I have graduated (ya soy graduado, importa hoy).
  • Pasado perfecto → antes de otro momento pasado: By 2024 I had already graduated.

La prueba del tiempo

Si hay una expresión de tiempo terminado (yesterday, in 2020, last year, when I was a child) → pasado simple. Si el periodo sigue abierto (today, this week, so far, this year) → presente perfecto.

En narración

She moved to Bogotá in 2019 (simple). She had lived in Cali before that (perfecto de pasado). She has lived there ever since (perfecto de presente).

Error frecuente

No se combina el presente perfecto con un momento pasado concreto: I have seen him yesterday es incorrecto.
lecciones.content_en:
Each with its reference point

  • Past simple → a finished past moment: I graduated in 2024.
  • Present perfect → connects with now: I have graduated (I am a graduate, it matters today).
  • Past perfect → before another past moment: By 2024 I had already graduated.

The time test

If there is a finished time expression (yesterday, in 2020, last year, when I was a child) → past simple. If the period is still open (today, this week, so far, this year) → present perfect.

In narration

She moved to Bogotá in 2019 (simple). She had lived in Cali before that (past perfect). She has lived there ever since (present perfect).

Common mistake

The present perfect is never combined with a specific past moment: I have seen him yesterday is wrong.

lecciones.t: for, since, already, yet, just, ever, never
lecciones.t_en: for, since, already, yet, just, ever, never
lecciones.content_es:
Duración

  • for + periodo: for two years, for a long time
  • since + punto de inicio: since 2020, since I was ten

Posición y uso

  • already: afirmativas, entre auxiliar y participio: I've already sent it.
  • yet: negativas y preguntas, al final: Haven't you finished yet?
  • just: acción muy reciente: She has just called.
  • ever: preguntas de experiencia: Have you ever lived abroad?
  • never: negativo por sí mismo: I've never tried it.
  • still: algo que continúa: I still haven't finished.

Ojo

since también puede introducir una oración: since I moved here. Y for se omite a veces con all: all my life, no for all my life.
lecciones.content_en:
Duration

  • for + period: for two years, for a long time
  • since + starting point: since 2020, since I was ten

Position and use

  • already: affirmatives, between auxiliary and participle: I've already sent it.
  • yet: negatives and questions, at the end: Haven't you finished yet?
  • just: a very recent action: She has just called.
  • ever: experience questions: Have you ever lived abroad?
  • never: negative on its own: I've never tried it.
  • still: something that continues: I still haven't finished.

Careful

since can also introduce a clause: since I moved here. And for is dropped with all: all my life, not for all my life.

lecciones.t: Saludos y comandos en registro académico
lecciones.t_en: Greetings and commands in an academic register
lecciones.content_es:
Registro formal escrito

Dear Ms. Ramírez, · I am writing to… · I would appreciate it if you could… · Thank you for your time. · Kind regards,

Registro oral formal

Good afternoon. Thank you for having me. · Allow me to introduce myself. · I would like to begin by…

Comandos académicos

Analyze the argument. · Evaluate the evidence. · Contrast both positions. · Justify your choice. · Cite the source. · Revise and edit your draft. · Proofread before submitting.

Ojo con el registro

  • Formal: I would like to… · Informal: I wanna… (no se usa por escrito)
  • Formal: Could you please…? · Informal: Can you…?

Proofread es revisar la ortografía y el formato; revise es reescribir el contenido.
lecciones.content_en:
Formal written register

Dear Ms. Ramírez, · I am writing to… · I would appreciate it if you could… · Thank you for your time. · Kind regards,

Formal spoken register

Good afternoon. Thank you for having me. · Allow me to introduce myself. · I would like to begin by…

Academic commands

Analyze the argument. · Evaluate the evidence. · Contrast both positions. · Justify your choice. · Cite the source. · Revise and edit your draft. · Proofread before submitting.

Careful with register

  • Formal: I would like to… · Informal: I wanna… (never in writing)
  • Formal: Could you please…? · Informal: Can you…?

Proofread is checking spelling and format; revise is rewriting the content.

lecciones.content_es:
Rasgos de carácter

resilient (resiliente), disciplined, adaptable, reliable, self-aware, humble, assertive (que se expresa con firmeza y respeto), persistent, open-minded, overwhelmed, indecisive.

Emociones con matiz

grateful, hopeful, uncertain, proud, ashamed, relieved, nostalgic, determined, fulfilled (realizado).

Reflexionar sobre la trayectoria

Looking back, I realize that… · What I've learned is… · That experience taught me to… · I used to be…, but I've become… · If I could go back, I would…

Estructuras útiles

  • have + participio para el balance: I have grown a lot.
  • used to para el contraste con antes.
  • I wish / If only para el arrepentimiento.
lecciones.content_en:
Character traits

resilient, disciplined, adaptable, reliable, self-aware, humble, assertive, persistent, open-minded, overwhelmed, indecisive.

Nuanced emotions

grateful, hopeful, uncertain, proud, ashamed, relieved, nostalgic, determined, fulfilled.

Reflecting on your path

Looking back, I realize that… · What I've learned is… · That experience taught me to… · I used to be…, but I've become… · If I could go back, I would…

Useful structures

  • have + participle for the balance: I have grown a lot.
  • used to for the contrast with the past.
  • I wish / If only for regret.

repaso.titulo: Repaso — Understanding the Past and Human Experiences
repaso.titulo_en: Review — Understanding the Past and Human Experiences
repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Tres tiempos compiten y cada uno tiene su punto de referencia: el pasado simple para lo cerrado, el presente perfecto para lo que conecta con hoy y el pasado perfecto para lo anterior a otro pasado. Las formas continuas añaden la idea de duración.

Puntos gramaticales

  • Con cantidad exacta → forma simple; con duración → forma continua.
  • Los verbos de estado no admiten formas continuas.
  • for + periodo; since + punto de inicio.
  • already en afirmativo, yet al final en negativos y preguntas, still antes del auxiliar.
  • El presente perfecto nunca va con un momento pasado concreto.

Vocabulario

Registro académico formal, comandos de análisis, rasgos de carácter y fórmulas de autorreflexión.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

Three tenses compete and each has its reference point: the past simple for what is closed, the present perfect for what connects with today and the past perfect for what came before another past. The continuous forms add the idea of duration.

Grammar points

  • With an exact quantity → simple form; with duration → continuous form.
  • State verbs take no continuous forms.
  • for + period; since + starting point.
  • already in affirmatives, yet at the end in negatives and questions, still before the auxiliary.
  • The present perfect never goes with a specific past moment.

Vocabulary

Formal academic register, analysis commands, character traits and self-reflection formulas.
puntos_clave: Periodo cerrado → pasado simple; abierto → presente perfecto.
Closed period → past simple; open period → present perfect.
Cantidad exacta pide la forma simple, no la continua.
An exact quantity calls for the simple form, not the continuous.
I have seen him yesterday es incorrecto.
I have seen him yesterday is incorrect.

proofread is form; revise is content.
